aggregates.text: GENERAL ELECTION, NOVEMBER 3RD, 2026. FOUR CERTIFIED TICKETS. BRONSON AND CHURCH. KREISS-TOMKINS AND JOHNSON. TAYLOR AND ENGLISH. WILSON AND SHOWER.
KREISS-TOMKINS AND JOHNSON LED THE PRIMARY WITH 37,006 VOTES, 22.5 PERCENT OF 164,303.
THE SIX ARE NOT THE SIX LARGEST DONORS. THE LARGEST SIX CARRY 24.38 PERCENT. ALSO HERE. AI FUTURES PROJECT $70,000. ALIGNMENT RESEARCH CENTER $20,000.
aggregates.note: the guard against conflating the six with the six largest donors. C41 has the 86 who gave over $4,000 as exactly the 86 largest, and the six are not among the top six of them.

aggregates.text: THE 105 LARGEST DONORS MATCH THE SIX.
aggregates.note: C14 counts DONORS grouped by name plus city plus state, summing to $372,960.85. The rings on this plate are the 105 largest GIFTS, which sum to $354,294.88, and the plate says both, because the sheet draws gifts and a donor may give twice.

aggregates.text: 2,705 of the 4,604 transactions came from Alaska addresses, 58.75 percent of them, carrying 26.56 percent of the money. The median Alaska gift is $50. California sent more, and it only sent more because six of its donors are on this sheet.
aggregates.note: transactions, not gifts. 16 of the 4,604 rows are refunds or adjustments per C42, so 58.75 percent is a share of rows.
what the ring cohort actually is, drawn from the transaction histogram. The donor-grouped claim is C14 and is carried in type on plate 01.

aggregates.text: 16 ALASKA GIFTS ABOVE THE LIMIT. 14 IN FRAME, DOTTED.
aggregates.note: the sheet draws gifts, so the dots mark the sixteen Alaska GIFTS above $4,000. C15's sixteen Alaska DONORS above $4,000 in aggregate is a donor-grouped figure this sheet's data cannot group, and it is carried in type by the headline's 86.
